Scene: night inside an old Japanese farmhouse after a spring supper. A tatami dining room with a
low dark wooden table: small ceramic side-dish bowls, one distinctive blue-and-white porcelain
bowl painted with small flowers, chopsticks on rests, a small vase of white spring wildflowers.
On the wooden step down to the earthen-floored kitchen, a shallow woven bamboo basket of fresh
wild greens with tiny white flowers. Paper shoji doors stand half open onto a dark garden where
a small mountain stream glints in the moonlight among young leaves. A warm paper lamp inside and
cold soft violet (#9B6BFF) moonlight outside. Quiet, homely, faintly uneasy. No person, no body.

Polished key-visual quality for a premium mystery adventure video game.
Composition: the key subjects are kept inside the central 60% of the width so the image can be
cropped to a narrower frame, with clean readable depth and atmospheric perspective.

Scene: early spring morning beside a small clear mountain stream in a damp broadleaf forest. The forest floor is a carpet of the small white-flowered anemone. In the foreground a woman seen from behind crouches and pinches ONE flowering stem between her fingers, laying it in a shallow woven bamboo basket already holding white-flowered stems. Right next to her hand grow a few clumps of the flowerless look-alike leaves, their outlines traced with a faint violet glow (the spot colour); her hand passes them by. A closed sketchbook and a pencil rest on a mossy rock beside the basket. Soft morning light, calm, careful, beautiful.

Botany to draw accurately: the edible spring wildflower is a low woodland anemone with small white five-petalled flowers held up on thin stalks, usually TWO flowers per stem, above a whorl of deeply three-parted, finely toothed soft leaves. The look-alike poisonous plant, not in flower in spring, has glossier palmately and deeply divided leaves of almost the same shape and size, growing mixed among the white-flowered plants; before flowering the two are very hard to tell apart.

Recurring characters in this story: the heroine is a Japanese woman in her late thirties with black hair loosely gathered at the nape with a pencil pushed through the knot, an unbleached linen shirt and an indigo work apron; she is only ever seen from behind or in silhouette. The other person who handles the plants is shown ONLY as hands and the cuffs of a dark cardigan (no face, no body). An old man in a flat cap and a woman with short hair appear only as small distant silhouettes.
